_doc: Camera choreography of /proto/: frame height (metres, world units) as a pure function of camera z.
Between focus windows the frame is `overview`; inside a window it eases to the focus frame and back.
Each focus is anchored to a stable layout object id; its world z (+ peak_offset) is where the focus peaks.
Window around the peak, along the route (z decreasing): approach metres ease in, hold metres (each side)
stay at the focus frame, exit metres ease out. Ease = smootherstep (no overshoot).
Limits: close <= frame <= overview (16..40 m) - the sprite pack has a resolution ceiling at 16 m.
The width follows from the viewport aspect in proto/main.js; nothing here assumes a screen size.
Checked by tools/camera_choreography.py (tests): anchors exist, route order, limits, no window overlaps a
biome transition's dim band, overview reached between windows.

focus.why: the lived-in village: tavern, lamp and road ('haggle and drink in taverns'); past the village card, so the card never covers it
the forest's one focal tree; kept at 24 m so the pines around it do not fill the frame
the mine entrance (timber adit + cart): the mine's main object
the crypt - 'death is a place'; left of the road, the spirit card sits right
the final house, whole in frame (22 m keeps it clear of the right-hand card)
